# Generator counts of groups generated by two subgroups are not always additive (Kourovka 12.71)

Write $d(X)$ for the minimal number of generators of a finite group $X$. There are finite groups
$A$ and $B$ such that for every finite group $G$ and all subgroups $H, K \le G$ with $H \cong A$,
$K \cong B$ and $\langle H, K \rangle = G$, we have $d(G) \ne d(A) + d(B)$.

Resolved false: the Kourovka Archive answers 12.71 "No, not always" (A. Lucchini, 2001). Since
$d(G) \le d(A) + d(B)$ always holds for such $G$, every finite group generated by subgroups
isomorphic to $A$ and $B$ needs fewer than $d(A) + d(B)$ generators (Kovács and Sim had shown this
within soluble groups).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.71 (L. Ribes); resolution: A. Lucchini, J. Group Theory 4 (2001), no. 1, 53-58, Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.71: No, not always.
